subject: Mid-contract capacity add: sizing and pricing options
messages:
From: Sophie Li <sophie.li@aihealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: procure@aihealth.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: mid-contract GPU add (+ throughput SLAs)

Hi Jonas,

We’re seeing an unexpected increase in inference traffic for our imaging triage models and need to add capacity mid-contract. Current environment: 120 A100-equivalent GPUs under our reserved pool with Redwood (commit until 2029-01). We’d like pricing and options for the following:

- Add 40 A100-equivalent GPUs to the same pool as a mid-term uplift, OR
- Convert a portion (40 GPUs) to a short-term reserved top-up (6–12 months) if a full-commit amendment is expensive.

Key asks:
- Target sustained throughput: ~6M tokens/min (across the new capacity) with 99th percentile latency target within our existing SLA window.
- Pricing delta for an uplift vs top-up (list per-GPU effective $/month and discount tiers at +25/40/80 GPUs).
- Impact on our existing commit (does price-step apply retroactively? any proration?).
- Timeline to have capacity online (we have a go-live target in 6 weeks).

Attached is a short requirements summary (aihealth_requirements.pdf). Procurement is looped (procure@aihealth.com) — they’ll need an estimate for the PO.

Can you share options and an indicative quote by EOD Monday?

Thanks,
Sophie Li
Head of Production
AiHealth Diagnostics

---
Attachment: aihealth_requirements.pdf (pdf, 48KB)
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Sophie Li <sophie.li@aihealth.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 12:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: mid-contract GPU add (+ throughput SLAs)

Hi Sophie — thanks for the detail and the attachment. We can support both approaches; below is an options summary and recommended path given your throughput and timeline.

Short summary of options (indicative):
1) Mid-contract amendment (recommended)
  - Add 40 GPUs to the reserved pool, amortize over remaining term or extend commitment by 12 months.
  - Indicative rate: $5,800/GPU/month list; effective price with uplift discounts:
    - +25 GPUs: 8% discount
    - +40 GPUs: 12% discount (applies to incremental GPUs)
    - +80 GPUs: 18% discount
  - Proration: we can pro-rate to the next billing cycle or align billing start to customer preference (see billing section).
  - SLA: We can guarantee throughput SLO for the combined pool; will require a short validation period (two-week throughput baseline) and an agreed runbook for burst behavior.

2) Short-term reserved top-up (6–12 months)
  - Higher per-GPU rate (~+10–15% vs mid-contract amendment) but no long-term extension required.
  - Good if you expect the traffic to be transient.

Technical considerations / recommended sizing:
- Given your 6M tokens/min target, adding 40 GPUs should meet the need assuming average 40–60 tokens/sec per GPU depending on sequence length and batching. If your sequences are long (>2k tokens), we should model effective throughput — I’ve asked Marcus to validate with your sample traces.
- We recommend enabling prefix KV caching for stable prompt distributions and a modest batching window (5–7ms) to preserve latency.

Timeline: provisioning pipeline for Dedicated additions is typically 2–4 weeks once PO/commit is final; we can fast-track to 10 business days for a mid-term amendment and reserved capacity if we align on sizing and payment terms.

Attached: redwood_draft_addendum_v2.docx (scope, pricing tables, proposed amendment language).

Next steps:
1) Marcus will run a quick throughput validation on your traces (can you share a sample trace set?)
2) We’ll draft a formal amendment (DocuSign) and an interim quote for procurement.
3) Confirm billing start date (prorated vs start-of-next-cycle).

Happy to jump on a quick call Monday if helpful.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 13:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: mid-contract GPU add (+ throughput SLAs)

Jonas / Laura — quick technical notes after scanning Sophie's requirements and the attachment:

- Workload shape: imaging triage tends to have heterogeneous sequence lengths (small metadata tokens + embedded image feature tokens). Effective tokens/sec per A100-equivalent will vary; plan for pessimistic 45 tokens/sec baseline per GPU for SLO planning.
- Batching: set a conservative batching cap for CPU/IO-bound preproc to avoid tail latency; continuous batching on the serving side is fine.
- KV cache: enable KV caching for repeated prefixes (we’ve seen 8–12% cost reduction in similar customers).
- Quantization: recommend 8-bit quantization for non-sensitive models — can free up ~20% effective throughput but requires QA.
- Node topology: prefer small, dense nodes (8-GPU pools) vs single large racks — gives faster scale-up and safer failure modes.

Commercial suggestion: approve a 10% introductory uplift discount for mid-contract additions (applies only to incremental GPUs for the first 3 months) to accelerate the PO, then revert to the +12% tier pricing after. This is a light concession that materially de-risks customer ramp.

I’ll stand by to run capacity modeling if Sophie can send a week of production traces (anonymized).

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
